questions.q: (a) Describe how to compare the population of dandelions on a sunny and a shady lawn using quadrats [4]. (b) Calculate the efficiency of transfer from grass (20 000 kJ) to rabbits (1600 kJ) [2]. (c) Name one abiotic factor that could explain a difference in the dandelion results [1].
questions.a: (a) random coordinates/quadrats in each area (1); same size and number of quadrats (1); count dandelions in each (1); calculate mean per quadrat and compare (1); (b) 1600 ÷ 20 000 × 100 = 8% (2); (c) light intensity (or water, temperature) (1)
questions.model: Teacher sets out (a): 'Use a random number table to place 10 quadrats in each area.'

questions.q: Explain how carbon in a rabbit's body can end up in a plant.
questions.a: Rabbit dies and is decomposed by microorganisms (1); they respire, releasing CO₂ (1); plants absorb CO₂ in photosynthesis (1)

questions.q: Why are pyramids of biomass usually pyramid-shaped but pyramids of number not always?
questions.a: One large producer (e.g. a tree) supports many consumers, but its biomass is still greater.

questions.q: Explain why energy transfer between trophic levels is inefficient.
questions.a: Energy used in respiration/lost as heat (1); not all parts eaten (bones, roots) (1); energy lost in faeces/urine (1)
questions.model: Three losses: respiration and heat, uneaten parts, and waste. Name each one.
